## 321729: locating colorings, two sustained mechanisms
Actual original1106.3453v3 defines the proper coloring as onto nonempty classes. On the rook graph K_m square K_n, every distinct nonadjacent pair is at distance two. For a proper matrix C with palette K, let M_i be colors missing from row i, N_j those missing from column j. The code of a cell with color a has coordinate0 at a, coordinate2 precisely on M_i intersection N_j, and coordinate1 elsewhere. Therefore C is locating iff, for each a, these intersection signatures are pairwise different over its occurrences. This pays the metric-to-matrix bridge exactly, not only a sufficient colorful-vertex test.

Route1 attempts an n+2 palette as a counterexample, i.e. two missing colors per row. For fixed row missing pair {x,y}, the signatures are {},{x},{y},{x,y}, according as its column contains both, just y, just x, or neither. For each color a at most one occurrence may have each given signature globally; row-pair labels vary, so merely counting four signatures per row is not a global contradiction. A cyclic Latin rectangle with K=n+2 and row shifts supplies properness when shifts are distinct, but does not automatically supply signatures. For example at n=m=6 and K=8, take entries i+j modulo8, indices0..5. The color5 occurs at (0,5),(1,4),(2,3),(3,2),(4,1),(5,0). Thus this natural specific construction fails symbolically without any enumeration. It lies in the conjectured range ceil(9/2)<6<=6 and supplies no counterexample.

Route2 seeks the n+3 upper construction by deleting three columns from a Latin square of order n+3, retaining m rows. Every row has a missing triple and every column has n+3-m missing colors. Properness is inherited. What remains is an exact choice of deleted columns/rows or switches such that all same-color intersections M_i intersection N_j are distinct, uniformly for ceil((n+3)/2)<m<=n. Cyclic choices repeat empty signatures just as above. Adding three singleton anchor colors to an n-color Latin square also does not solve this: a singleton cell only records whether a vertex shares its row/column, so three anchors separate at most seven rows by incidence and leave many repeated signatures for large m. A useful repair would require distributed anchor classes, not singleton anchors.
